We are allowed to delete any elements from each array, exactly half of each array's length. Equivalent to selecting n/2 elements from each array to keep (since total length n, remove n/2, keep n/2). So from each array we must keep exactly n/2 elements (we can choose which). After keeping, we union them into a set.

We want to maximize the size of the union of kept elements from both arrays.

Thus we can think: we have two multisets (arrays). We need to choose subsets A ⊆ nums1 of size n/2, and B ⊆ nums2 of size n/2, to maximize |A ∪ B|.

We can choose any elements (including duplicates). However duplicates in the kept arrays don't increase set size beyond one per distinct value.

Observation: To maximize union size, we generally want to keep as many distinct elements as possible from both arrays, but we are limited by the number of slots we can keep: n/2 from each array.

If there were no overlap between nums1 and nums2 distinct values, we could keep up to n/2 distinct from each, total up to n distinct. But we have only n elements kept total (n/2 + n/2 = n). Actually we keep n elements total (since each array kept n/2). The maximum possible union size is at most n (if all kept elements are distinct). However we may have duplicates across arrays limiting.

We need to consider overlap: elements that appear in both arrays. If we keep an element that appears in both arrays, it may be counted only once in union, wasting a slot that could have been used for a distinct element only present in one array.

Thus we want to avoid keeping duplicates across arrays as much as possible, prefer to keep distinct elements unique to each array.

But we also have constraints: we must keep exactly n/2 elements from each array, we may be forced to keep some duplicates if there aren't enough unique elements.
